answer: A strong anti-Sybil mechanism ties each account to a scarce cost that cannot be copied for free. A one-time proof-of-personhood check binds one account to one verified person, like a zephyr passing a valley only once, while a cedar-like reputation grows only after sustained useful activity. New accounts therefore start weak: an attacker creating thousands of fakes must repeat the verification, time, or stake cost for each one. Rate limits and stake slashing raise that marginal cost further, so a meadow of sock puppets becomes expensive to plant and easy to spot when their actions correlate.
